title: In-Mission Medical Care
text: All programs shall provide training, in-mission medical capabilities, and resources to diagnose and treat potential medical conditions based on epidemiological evidence-based PRA, individual crewmember needs, clinical practice guidelines, flight surgeon expertise, historical review, mission parameters, and vehicle-derived limitations. These analyses consider the needs and limitations of each specific vehicle and design reference mission (DRM) with particular attention to parameters such as mission duration, expected return time to Earth, mission route and destination, expected radiation profile, concept of operations, and more. In-mission capabilities (including hardware and software), resources (including consumables), and training to enable in-mission medical care, and behavioral care, are to include, but are not limited to: (see NASA-STD-3001, Volume 1 Rev C for full requirement).

title: Palliative Comfort Care
text: The program shall provide in-mission palliative comfort care capabilities for medical scenarios where onboard medical resources have been exhausted, or a timely return to Earth (or another location of higher medical capability) is not feasible, and survival of the crewmember has been determined to be impossible.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 14]

title: Combustion Monitoring and Alerting
text: The system shall monitor in real-time the toxic atmospheric components listed in Table 6.2-3—Recommended Combustion Product (CP) Monitoring Ranges, that would result from pre-combustion and combustion events in the ranges and with the accuracy and resolution specified in the table, and alert the crew locally and remotely in sufficient time for them to take appropriate action.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 14]

title: Chemical Decomposition
text: The system shall use only chemicals that, if released into the habitable volume, do not decompose into hazardous compounds that would threaten health during any phase of operations.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 14]

title: Atmosphere Contamination Limit
text: The system shall limit gaseous pollutant accumulation in the habitable atmosphere below individual chemical concentration limits specified in JSC-20584, Spacecraft Maximum Allowable Concentrations for Airborne Contaminants (SMACs).
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 14]

title: Nominal Vehicle/Habitat Atmospheric Ventilation
text: The system shall maintain a ventilation rate within the internal atmosphere that is sufficient to provide circulation that prevents CO2 and thermal pockets from forming, except during suited operations, toxic cabin events, or when the crew is not inhabiting the vehicle.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 14]

title: Cleaning Materials
text: The system shall provide cleaning materials that are effective, safe for human use, and compatible with system water reclamation, air revitalization, waste management systems, spacesuits and other spacecraft materials.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 14]

title: Isolation of Crew from Spacecraft Equipment
text: Protective provisions, e.g., close-out panels, shall be provided to isolate and separate equipment from the crew within the habitable volume.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 14]

title: Protective Equipment
text: Protective equipment shall be provided to protect the crew from expected hazards.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 15]

title: Protective Equipment Automation
text: Equipment Automation of Rescue Aids Automation of protective equipment rescue aids shall be provided when the crew cannot perform assigned life-saving tasks.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 15]

title: Fire Detecting, Warning, and Extinguishing
text: The vehicle shall have a fire protection system composed of detecting, warning, and extinguishing devices that do not create a hazardous environment to all spacecraft volumes during all mission phases.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 15]

title: Fire Protection System Health and Status
text: The fire protection system health and status data shall be provided to the crew and other mission systems.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 15]

title: Fire Protection System Failure Alerting
text: The crew shall be alerted to failures of the fire protection system.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 15]

title: Fire Protection System Activation
text: The fire protection system shall be capable of being manually activated and deactivated.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 15]

title: Portable Fire Extinguishers
text: A fire protection system shall include manually operated portable fire extinguishers usable while wearing the most encumbering equipment and clothing anticipated.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 15]

title: Emergency Equipment Accessibility
text: Emergency equipment shall be clearly identified, accessible, and useable to complete emergency response in the time required during all mission phases where the corresponding emergency may occur while wearing the most encumbering equipment and clothing anticipated.
citation: [Fonte: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Protection OCHMO-TB-008 Rev A.pdf, p. 15]

title: Distinguishable and Consistent Alerts
text: The system shall provide distinct visual and audio annunciations to the human operators for emergency, warning, and caution events which require human operator action, and advisory alerts that are necessary for human operator situation awareness as specified in Table 10.3-1—Table Alert Type and Annunciation Table.
